content: Dogs should be fed 2 times per day for adults, and 3-4 times per day for puppies under 6 months. Avoid feeding within 1 hour before or after vigorous exercise to prevent bloat. Fresh water should always be available.

Adult cats typically need 2 meals per day. Kittens under 6 months need 3-4 small meals. Cats are obligate carnivores and require taurine from animal protein. Wet food supports hydration, especially for cats prone to urinary issues.

Most adult dogs need 30-60 minutes of exercise daily. High-energy breeds like Border Collies or Huskies may need 1-2 hours. Senior dogs benefit from shorter, gentle walks. Puppies should follow the 5-minute rule per month of age, twice daily.

Cats need 10-15 minutes of active play twice daily. Interactive toys like feather wands or laser pointers stimulate their natural hunting instinct. Indoor cats especially need enrichment to prevent obesity and boredom.

Dogs should be bathed every 4-6 weeks depending on coat type and activity level. Brush short-haired dogs weekly and long-haired dogs 3-4 times per week. Nails should be trimmed every 3-4 weeks. Ears should be checked weekly for debris or odor.

Short-haired cats typically groom themselves but benefit from weekly brushing to reduce hairballs. Long-haired cats need daily brushing to prevent mats. Nails should be trimmed every 2-3 weeks. Most cats do not need baths unless medically necessary.

Rabbits should have unlimited access to fresh hay (timothy or orchard grass), which should make up 80% of their diet. Fresh leafy greens like romaine, kale, and cilantro should be offered daily (1 cup per 2 lbs body weight). Pellets should be limited to 1/4 cup per 5 lbs of body weight daily.
Rabbits need at least 3-4 hours of free-roaming time outside their enclosure daily. They are most active at dawn and dusk. Tunnels, cardboard boxes, and toys help encourage natural behaviors.

Parrots and pet birds should eat a varied diet of pellets (60-70%), fresh vegetables (20-30%), and limited seeds or fruits as treats. Fresh food should be removed after 2-4 hours to prevent spoilage. Avoid avocado, chocolate, onion, and caffeine, which are toxic to birds.

Most freshwater fish should be fed once or twice daily with only as much food as they can consume in 2-3 minutes. Overfeeding degrades water quality. Fasting fish one day per week is beneficial for digestion.

Dogs should visit the vet for an annual wellness exam. Core vaccinations include rabies (every 1-3 years), DHPP (distemper, hepatitis, parvo, parainfluenza) annually or every 3 years. Heartworm prevention should be given monthly. Flea and tick prevention is recommended year-round in most climates.

Cats need an annual wellness exam. Core vaccines include rabies and FVRCP (feline viral rhinotracheitis, calicivirus, panleukopenia). Indoor cats still need vaccinations and parasite prevention. Senior cats (7+) benefit from bi-annual checkups.

Dogs should have their teeth brushed at least 2-3 times per week, ideally daily. Dental chews, water additives, and veterinary dental cleanings (typically annually for adults) help prevent periodontal disease, which affects 80% of dogs by age 3.
Cats are prone to dental disease; teeth brushing 2-3 times weekly is ideal. Dental treats and regular vet cleanings help. Signs of dental problems include bad breath, drooling, or difficulty eating.

All pets need access to clean, fresh water daily. Water bowls should be washed and refilled every day. Fountain-style waterers can encourage cats and dogs to drink more. Signs of dehydration include lethargy, sunken eyes, and dry gums.

Mental enrichment is as important as physical exercise. Puzzle feeders, training sessions, rotating toys, and social interaction all prevent boredom and behavioral issues. Enrichment is especially important for intelligent breeds and indoor pets.
